findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "build_swap_transaction" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_api_access" references sensitive artifacts (apikey). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: How to use Realtap's API at higher rates: the anonymous limit, how to get a free key without a wallet (Telegram /apikey), the key's limits, request credits in A…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_token_safety" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
